Reflective Journal

Weekly reflections from Mohsin's handwritten Internship Reflective Log, kept across the three weeks of the placement.

Week 1

30 September – 02 October

What did I learn this week?

This week I learned how to manage a classroom and how to explain lessons in a simple and easy way. I learned how to communicate with students, keep them engaged, and plan a lesson before class. I also learned the importance of patience, discipline and time management in teaching.

What can I do differently tomorrow?

Tomorrow I will try to be more confident and interactive. I will ask more questions, use more examples and give students more time to speak in class. I will also prepare my lesson earlier so I can manage time better.

Week 2

05 October – 09 October

What did I learn this week?

I supported Mathematics work on counting and number recognition. I learned that language learning requires patience and individual attention, and that examples from daily life can make lessons more meaningful. I learned that checking notebooks and listening to students helps identify their learning difficulties.

What can I do differently tomorrow?

I will encourage more students to read aloud and respond. I will use clear examples and check each student's written work. I will give extra support to students who need more reading practice, and ask questions that connect lesson topics with students' surroundings.

Week 3

03 November – 06 November

What did I learn this week?

I learned that regular reading and encouragement help students become more confident. I learned that students benefit when mistakes are corrected step by step, and that students progress at different speeds and need supportive guidance.

What can I do differently tomorrow?

I will explain difficult questions slowly and allow students time to practise. I will remain patient and make sure every learner gets a chance. In future, I will plan activities carefully and keep improving my teaching skills.

Internship Report

School Teaching Internship — Government Boys Primary School Balach Khan Khoso, Taluka Qubo Saeed Khan · SEMIS Code 427050171, with M A English Coaching Centre, Qubo Saeed Khan.

1. Introduction

Teaching internship is an important part of teacher education. It provides an opportunity to connect theoretical knowledge with practical classroom experience. Through school-based teaching practice, an intern becomes familiar with classroom teaching, lesson planning, student learning needs, classroom management, assessment and the day-to-day responsibilities of a teacher.

I, Mohsin Ali Brohi, completed a 96-hour teaching internship over 12 days. Each day included 5 hours at Government Boys Primary School Balach Khan Khoso, Taluka Qubo Saeed Khan, and 3 hours at M A English Coaching Centre, Qubo Saeed Khan. During the internship, I observed and supported primary classroom teaching and English teaching-learning activities. This report describes the placements, activities performed, skills developed, challenges and learning outcomes.

2. Host Institution

Government Boys Primary School Balach Khan Khoso is a government primary school located in Taluka Qubo Saeed Khan, Sindh. The school provides primary education from Grade 1 to Grade 5. The subjects taught at the school include Sindhi, English, Mathematics, Urdu, Social Studies, Science and Islamiyat. The school operates from 8:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. The internship provided an opportunity to observe the school's daily routine, classroom arrangements, teaching methods and student participation.

3. Internship Objectives

The main objective of the internship was to understand the responsibilities of a primary-school teacher and gain practical experience in a real classroom. The specific objectives were to observe classroom teaching, support lesson delivery, understand students' learning needs, practise clear communication, assist with classwork and assessment, and develop classroom-management and professional skills.

4. Activities During the Internship

The internship activities included observing the school routine, morning assembly, classroom arrangements and students' learning levels. I assisted the class teacher with attendance and classroom organization. I supported English lessons through alphabet revision, simple words, oral reading and short questions. I also supported Mathematics lessons on counting, number recognition and simple addition through board and notebook exercises. The daily placement schedule consisted of 5 hours at the government primary school and 3 hours at M A English Coaching Centre, making 8 hours per day and 96 hours across 12 days.

I helped students with Sindhi and Urdu reading, handwriting and sentence practice. I assisted with Science and general knowledge activities through classroom discussion, question-answer and familiar examples from daily life. At the coaching centre I taught English grammar — Parts of Speech (noun, pronoun, adjective, verb, adverb, preposition, conjunction, interjection) and Tenses, including the Present Simple Tense. I reviewed students' classwork, helped learners who needed additional support, maintained learning materials and discussed students' progress with the class teacher.

5. Teaching Methods and Learning Materials

Primary students learn effectively when lessons are explained in simple language and connected with familiar examples. During the internship, I observed and supported explanation, demonstration, question-answer, reading aloud, repetition, individual practice and board work. Learning materials included textbooks, the whiteboard, students' notebooks and classroom resources such as charts and number cards. Activities were kept suitable for the students' grade and learning level.

6. Classroom Management and Student Participation

A positive classroom environment is created when students feel safe, respected and encouraged to participate. Clear instructions, fair treatment, positive encouragement and well-organized activities help maintain discipline. Students have different learning speeds, so repetition, examples, individual guidance and checking notebooks can help address their learning needs.

7. Skills Developed

The internship helped develop communication skills, lesson-support skills, classroom observation, classroom management, time management, assessment, teamwork, patience and professional responsibility. Supporting different subjects also improved my ability to explain basic concepts and guide students during reading, writing and number activities.

8. Challenges Faced

Primary students may have different levels of understanding and need different kinds of support. Some students require repeated explanations, while others complete activities quickly. Maintaining attention and ensuring participation from all students can also be challenging. These challenges can be addressed through simple explanations, short activities, positive encouragement, individual support and careful classroom organization.

9. Learning Outcomes

The internship helped me understand the daily responsibilities of a primary-school teacher. I learned that effective teaching requires preparation, clear communication, patience and awareness of students' learning needs. I also learned the value of classroom observation, questioning, checking students' work and providing constructive feedback. The experience strengthened my confidence and understanding of the teaching-learning process.

10. Conclusion and Suggestions

Overall, the 96-hour internship across Government Boys Primary School Balach Khan Khoso and M A English Coaching Centre, Qubo Saeed Khan, was a valuable learning experience. It provided practical exposure to the primary-school environment and English coaching activities and helped me develop important teaching and professional skills. I am thankful to the administrators and teachers at both placements for providing opportunities to observe and support learning activities.

It is suggested that interns receive guidance in lesson planning, classroom observation and assessment, and have opportunities to practise teaching under the supervision of experienced teachers. Simple charts, worksheets and other teaching-learning materials can further support classroom learning.
